title: Hierarchical QoS-driven phase split and token-budget arbitration for prefill/decode
creator: Asha Menon
description: Problem: Our current prefill/decode scheduler applies a flat fairness policy which causes latency-sensitive low-token requests to compete poorly with high-throughput batch jobs. This manifests as p99 decode latency regressions for interactive clients during sustained high-throughput prefills. Goal: Introduce a hierarchical QoS layer that splits work into prefill and decode phases and enforces token-budget arbitration across QoS classes so we can prioritize latency-critical decode work without starving throughput-oriented workloads. This ticket covers design, short experiments, and a first-pass rollout on canary hosts.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can tag requests with QoS class (interactive, standard, background) at ingress
Phase-split accounting separate prefill and decode token budgets per worker
High-priority interactive traffic achieves p95 decode latency <= 120ms on target hardware under mixed load
Throughput jobs retain >=80% baseline token/sec on best-effort pools after QoS enforcement
No user-visible request reordering for requests within same QoS class (stability guarantee)
proposed_design: Ingress tagging: API layer assigns QoS based on plan, route, and request metadata; default=standard
Hierarchical token budgets: each worker maintains a local budget bucket per phase (prefill, decode) and per QoS class; budgets refill based on configurable rate-limits and token credits
Soft deadlines & token credits: interactive requests get 'decode credits' that preempt best-effort prefill tokens up to a configurable cap to bound tail latency impact

Phase-aware arbitration: scheduler enforces that decode phase tokens are considered separately and have higher selection weight for interactive QoS; prefill tokens can be throttled/backpressured when decode budgets are low
Backpressure propagation: when local budgets are exhausted, worker sends a lightweight signal to fronting router to push new low-priority requests to spillover pools

Integration with kernel selection: for decode-phase with interactive QoS, prefer low-latency kernels (smaller optimized GEMM paths) and attention kernels tuned for short sequences to reduce token latency
Attention opt heuristics: prefill jobs longer than threshold can use chunked attention kernels and KV compression; decode-critical streams avoid chunking to reduce per-token jitter
Metrics & telemetry hooks: emit token accounting per-phase, per-QoS and allocate traces for p50/p95/p99 by phase
tradeoffs_and_risks: Risk: Strict QoS enforcement may reduce overall throughput; mitigated by hierarchical budgets and burst credits
Risk: Additional bookkeeping increases per-request overhead; mitigated by batching budget operations and approximate counters
Tradeoff: Prefill kernel selection for throughput may diverge from decode kernel path, adding complexity to cache warming and binary selection
Operational risk: Mis-tagged QoS could lead to unfair advantage; add monitoring and alerting on QoS distribution changes
experiments: Small canary: run hierarchical budget logic on 10% of low-latency cluster with synthetic mix (70% prefills long, 30% interactive) and compare p95/p99 decode vs baseline
Kernel experiment: A/B decode kernel selection for interactive QoS to measure delta in per-token latency and throughput impact
Budget tuning sweep: vary decode credit cap and refill rate to find knee where interactive p99 stabilizes without >20% throughput regression
Attention opt validation: run ensembles with chunked attention on long sequences and compare memory/throughput gains vs decode jitter
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Deploy scheduler feature flag to 10% of serving nodes for 72h, observe metrics and errors
Phase 2 (limited): Expand to 33% after fixes and implement automatic mitigation to disable budget enforcement if p50 decode degrades >10%
Phase 3 (full): Global rollout with adjustable knobs surfaced in Console and default conservative budget values
Fallback: automatic downgrade to flat fairness policy triggered by health checks if queue saturation or increased tail errors are detected
dependencies: ENG-28410: lightweight ingress QoS tags and plan lookup
ENG-29850: kernel registry flagging for latency-optimized kernels
PM-207: console knobs for scheduling parameters
blockers: Need kernel registry flagging merged (ENG-29850) before decode kernel selection experiment
KV cache accounting hook required (ENG-30111) to correctly charge prefill vs decode tokens
